Health of the posterior weights behind a BFRS calibration

Source: R/calc_weight_health.R
calc_weight_health.Rd

Draws are sampled from the prior and scored by the log-likelihood \(\ell\), so the posterior weights of the draws are a coarsened (generalised-Bayes) likelihood, \(w_i \propto \exp\{\eta(\ell_i - \max_j \ell_j)\}\), with \(\eta = \alpha / n_{obs}\): \(\alpha\) (coarsening_alpha) is the effective number of independent observations the likelihood is trusted with and \(n_{obs}\) the number of scored observation cells (Miller and Dunson 2019; Bissiri, Holmes and Walker 2016). \(\eta\) is fixed before the weights are seen, so the ESS of these weights is not circular.

The result holds:

coarsened

The posterior over every valid draw: eta, ess_kish (ESS_all), ess_prop, the largest weight share, khat (Pareto k-hat of the tempered weights, calc_is_diagnostics(eta * log_lik)) with khat_status, and khat_trend / khat_trend_slope (whether k-hat falls as draws accumulate, .mosaic_khat_trend()); n_locations and alpha_per_location (\(\eta\) is pooled over locations).

bestfit

The best-fit ensemble: draws in descending log-likelihood until their subset ESS reaches best_subset_ratio * ESS_all, bounded by [min_members, max_members]. Members (idx, sim), their renormalised weights, ess_best, mass (posterior weight held), binding and capped.

mce

Monte Carlo standard error of the members' posterior means per parameter (seed batches by (sim - 1) mod n_batches; SD of the batch means / posterior SD / \(\sqrt{B'}\), over the \(B'\) batches holding at least 1 percent of the members' weight), with median, p90 and max.

informativeness

The N-invariant informativeness measure: ess_untempered (Kish ESS of the untempered, \(\eta = 1\), weights), ess_untempered_frac (that ESS / valid draws), n_tied_max (valid draws tied at the best log-likelihood) and flat_ess_frac (the threshold). flat is ess_untempered_frac >= flat_ess_frac, NA when not assessable (fewer than 1 / flat_ess_frac valid draws).

eta_star

A diagnostic only (since red-team round 1): the largest \(\eta \le 1\) at which the Kish ESS over all draws still reaches the ESS_all target (ess_best_target / best_subset_ratio), by bisection on \(\log\eta\); n_eff = n_obs * eta. It grows with the draws, so it no longer decides flatness.

slope

The log-log ESS growth slope, supplied by the caller from a batch history (NA for a single snapshot).

convergence

The calc_convergence_status result (through .mosaic_health_status()); status and reasons repeat its colour and its reasons (joined by "; ").

context

budget_exhausted, fixed_mode and n_attempted, so the status can be re-derived for other members.

The \(\eta = 1\) likelihood-concentration numbers are not part of this result (they are in convergence_diagnostics.json only, from calc_is_diagnostics), nor is the all-draws seed-batch ratio.

No Monte Carlo-noise ceiling is applied to \(\eta^*\). It would be \(\eta \le 1.7/\sigma_{seed}\), where \(\sigma_{seed}\) is the seed-to-seed SD of the log-likelihood at fixed parameters (Doucet et al. 2015), which needs per-replicate log-likelihoods that run_MOSAIC() collapses by log-mean-exp and does not store.

Usage

calc_weight_health(
  log_lik,
  weights = NULL,
  params,
  n_obs,
  sim = NULL,
  coarsening_alpha = 10,
  best_subset_ratio = 0.2,
  ess_best_target = 200,
  min_members = 30L,
  max_members = 1000L,
  n_batches = 10L,
  thresholds = list(),
  slope = NA_real_,
  budget_exhausted = FALSE,
  fixed_mode = FALSE,
  n_attempted = NULL,
  n_locations = NULL,
  ess_all_target = NULL,
  max_simulations = NULL,
  batch_size_min = 500L,
  batch_size_max = 10000L,
  ess_target = NULL,
  batch_max = NULL,
  ess_method = NULL
)

Arguments

log_lik

Numeric vector of per-draw log-likelihoods. Non-finite entries get zero weight.

weights, ess_target, batch_max, ess_method

Deprecated since MOSAIC 1.4.0 and ignored (with a warning): the posterior summaries use the best-fit members, the ESS target is ess_best_target, the Monte Carlo error bands replace the batch-ratio limit, and the \(\eta = 1\) block is gone.

params

Data frame or matrix of sampled parameter values, one row per draw. Non-numeric columns and columns constant over the valid draws are dropped.

n_obs

Number of scored observation cells (see calc_run_weight_health()); sets \(\eta = \alpha / n_{obs}\).

sim

Simulation ids, one per draw (seed batches and selection ties). Default seq_along(log_lik).

coarsening_alpha

Positive number: the effective number of independent observations of the posterior. Default 10.

best_subset_ratio

Share of ESS_all the best-fit ensemble must reach, in (0, 1]. Default 0.2.

ess_best_target

Required ensemble ESS. Default 200.

min_members, max_members

Bounds on the ensemble size. Defaults 30 and 1000.

n_batches

Number of seed batches. Default 10.

thresholds

Named list overriding the status bands (see calc_convergence_status).

slope

Log-log ESS growth slope over recent batches (from run_state.json); NA for a single snapshot.

budget_exhausted

Logical; the run stopped at its simulation cap.

fixed_mode

Logical; a fixed-budget run (the status is assessed, not used to stop).

n_attempted

Simulations attempted, valid or not (converts projected valid draws to simulations). Default NULL: length(log_lik).

n_locations

Number of locations in the run (recorded with alpha_per_location; \(\eta\) is pooled over locations). Default NULL (unknown).

ess_all_target

ESS_all target of the reasons and projections. Default NULL: ess_best_target / best_subset_ratio (the best-fit rule). Under "coarsened" pass the scheme's own target (the resample size, so about ess_best_target).

max_simulations

The run's max_simulations_total (adaptive), so the k-hat reason can say whether its projection is within the budget. Default NULL (unknown).

batch_size_min, batch_size_max

batch_size_adaptive and max_batch_predictive: bound the confirming batch included in sims_projected_for_green. Defaults 500 and 10,000.

Value

A list with elements n_draws, n_valid, targets, coarsened, bestfit, mce, informativeness, eta_star, slope, flat, context, convergence, status ("green", "yellow" or "red") and reasons (one string).

Details

Computes every quantity behind the MOSAIC 1.4.0 simulation-convergence status from the scored draws, and the status itself through calc_convergence_status (the only place the rule lives). The calculation changes no weight, subset or posterior.

References

Miller JW, Dunson DB (2019). Robust Bayesian inference via coarsening. JASA 114(527):1113-1125.

Bissiri PG, Holmes CC, Walker SG (2016). A general framework for updating belief distributions. JRSS B 78(5):1103-1130.

Doucet A, Pitt MK, Deligiannidis G, Kohn R (2015). Efficient implementation of Markov chain Monte Carlo when using an unbiased likelihood estimator. Biometrika 102(2):295-313.

See also

calc_convergence_status, calc_run_weight_health

Other calibration-metrics: calc_convergence_diagnostics(), calc_convergence_status(), calc_model_agreement_index(), calc_model_cvw(), calc_model_ess(), calc_run_weight_health()

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 20000
theta <- runif(n)
ll <- -2e5 * (theta - 0.4)^2            # a likelihood over 100,000 cells
wh <- calc_weight_health(ll, params = data.frame(theta = theta), n_obs = 1e5)
wh$bestfit$ess_best
#> [1] 999.9865
wh$status
#> [1] "green"
wh$convergence$checks
#>             check                               label         value
#> 1             ess                        Ensemble ESS 999.986519079
#> 2             mce Monte Carlo error (90th percentile)   0.020762833
#> 3            khat       Validity guard (Pareto k-hat)  -1.793246790
#> 4 informativeness                Data informativeness   0.005554321
#>   threshold_green threshold_yellow colour
#> 1           2e+02           100.00  green
#> 2           1e-01             0.15  green
#> 3           5e-01             0.70  green
#> 4           1e-02               NA  green
#>                                                                                                                  reason
#> 1                                                                                             ensemble ESS 1,000 >= 200
#> 2 Monte Carlo standard error of the posterior means 2.1% of the posterior SD (90th percentile over parameters) <= 10.0%
#> 3                                                                      Pareto k-hat of the tempered weights -1.79 < 0.5
#> 4                             the data inform the posterior (the untempered likelihood ESS is 0.56% of the draws, < 1%)
